content.title: Steepening of U.S. Treasury Yield Curve Remains in Market's Focus
content.summary: The focus in U.S. Treasurys is on the steepening yield curve as further Federal Reserve rate cuts are seen next year, Saxo's strategy team said in a note.  While the two-year benchmark Treasury yield remains anchored near 3.50%, the 10-year Treasury yield is hovering around close to the recent three-month high of just above 4.20%.  Last Friday, the yield spread between the 10-year and two-year Treasury yields closed above 66 basis points for the first time in 2025, the steepest the yield curve has been since early 2022, they said.

content.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Fall Ahead of Key Labor Market Data
content.summary: U.S. Treasury yields declined in Asian afternoon trade, with the market anticipating that fresh data will confirm labor market weakness. "Given the Federal Reserve's increased focus on the labor market, today's labor market statistics for October and November may well be market moving, should they fall outside consensus estimates," Danske Bank Research's Jens Peter Sorensen said in a note.
